newsitem.title: USA: Jerusalem mayor says no regrets on tunnel opening.
newsitem.headline: Jerusalem mayor says no regrets on tunnel opening.

text.p: Jerusalem Mayor Ehud Olmert said on Tuesday he had no regrets about the opening of a tunnel in his city which led to bloody clashes last month, killing 59 Palestinians and 15 Israelis.

"I think it was the right thing to do," Olmert told Reuters as he was leaving a gala reception in New York on the eve of the Israel-North America Business conference intended to spark U.S. investment in Israeli infrastructure.
Olmert said he had been surprised by the outbreak of violence after the archaeological tunnel near Islamic sites in Arab East Jerusalem was opened.

"I did not expect this type of violence, but the fact that it happened doesn't mean that the opening of the tunnel was not correct," he said. "It just proves that our neighbours have to be more restrained and they have to teach themselves to adjust to the realities of life."
The violence led to a hastily convened summit which brought Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to Washington.
Tuesday's reception was also attended by Israel's Minister of National Infrastructures Ariel Sharon and New York Mayor Rudolph Giuliani.
